comment: Engine choices of SlicerX for an opened project. keeps: stay when a project opens, unless the person changed them in the project (its different_settings_to_system lists the key); over, when given, names the only inherited values a keep replaces, so any other value the project inherited stays its own (a project that does not set the key still gets the keep); exceptPrinters, when given, names the printers whose projects the keep leaves alone (the project's printer_model starts with one), so they keep the value they inherited; note says what the open kept when the project's inherited value differs. defaults: apply only when the project does not set the key at all, whatever app wrote it; a value the project sets is its own (projectDefaults requests take fromApp only). fromApp: by the app that wrote the file (the model's Application metadata starts with the name), its reading of keys its project lacks: each applies only when the project does not set the key, nor any key in unlessAny. A row with sameAs is that key's value instead (value when the project lacks that key too), whatever the project sets. The app, the MCP server (engine-choices.ts) and sx slice <project.3mf> (sx-core, through build.rs) all read this file. value: what SlicerX prints with.

wall_generator.note: Kept SlicerX's aegis walls; the project used its preset's default.

support_top_z_distance.note: A project that does not set its support gaps slices with the schema's 0.2 mm, as it opens in the app, not one layer as a request with only a layer height gets.

support_bottom_z_distance.note: The same for the gap under supports that stand on the part.

initial_layer_travel_acceleration.note: Bambu Studio reads a missing first layer travel acceleration as 500 mm/s2, not as a share of the travel acceleration.

internal_bridge_speed.note: Its presets have no internal bridge speed, and it prints internal bridges at the bridge speed, not our 150 percent.

wipe_tower_wall_type.note: A project saved before the rib wall switch existed has neither key: the rib wall, that app's default.

solid_infill_direction.note: Bambu Studio has no solid infill direction of its own: its infill direction sets the solid and the sparse lines alike, so a value the project holds is not read.
